cards.text: Nehemiah tells this one himself. He serves King Artaxerxes, and the king has sent him to Jerusalem, the city where his fathers are buried (Nehemiah 2:1-6). He's been there three days, and friend, I can't last three MINUTES without opening the oven to peek at a batch.

cards.question: Nehemiah finally heads out to look around Jerusalem with just a few men. When does he go?
God has laid something on Nehemiah's heart to do for Jerusalem. Who has Nehemiah told about it?

cards.text: Just Nehemiah and a few men, the quietest parade in history. Out through the Valley Gate he goes, toward the Well of the Serpent and the Dung Gate.

cards.question: Riding out in the dark, Nehemiah inspects the broken-down walls of Jerusalem and the ___ that were destroyed by fire.

cards.text: Next comes the Fountain Gate and the King's Pool, and right there the night tour hits a snag. You know when your GPS says "turn here" and there is NO here?

cards.question: Nehemiah reaches the Fountain Gate and the King's Pool, but there's no room for his ___ to get through.

cards.text: So he goes up the valley by night, inspects the wall and comes back in through the Valley Gate, and the officials have NO clue where he went or what he was doing. Friend, I spent YEARS in the dark of a junk drawer by accident, so a man who keeps everybody in the dark on PURPOSE has my respect.
Then Nehemiah finally speaks up, and he starts with the hard truth: “Jerusalem lies in ruins, and its gates have been burned down.”

cards.question: Jerusalem is in ruins and its gates are burned. What does Nehemiah say he and the people should do about it?

answers.text: Ask the king to send builders

cards.question: Nehemiah says that if they rebuild the wall, he and the people will no longer be a disgrace.

cards.text: Then he tells them about the gracious hand of his God on him. And he tells them what the king said, which is like walking into a work meeting where the big boss ALREADY signed off on your plan.

cards.question: After hearing about God's gracious hand and the king's words, the people tell Nehemiah they need time to think it over.

cards.text: The people set their hands to this good work. Then word gets to Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite official and Geshem the Arab.

cards.question: What do Sanballat, Tobiah and Geshem do when they hear about the rebuilding?

answers.text: Offer to help with the wall

cards.question: Sanballat, Tobiah and Geshem ask the builders if they are ___ against the king.
Nehemiah answers the mockers. Who does he say will grant the builders success?
Nehemiah tells Sanballat, Tobiah and Geshem that they have a claim in Jerusalem too.

cards.text: Then the rebuilding starts, crew next to crew, from Eliashib the high priest and his fellow priests at the Sheep Gate all the way around until the last stretch meets the Sheep Gate again. The crews include goldsmiths and perfumers, and Shallum, a ruler in Jerusalem, works with the help of his daughters. Goldsmiths and perfumers on a wall crew, friend, that's like your dentist showing up to help put on your new roof, and I LOVE it. The Tekoites' nobles, though, don't put their shoulders to the work.
And that's where we'll leave the wall for now, but trust me, friend, this story is NOT done yet.
